readout_other: MR acoustic radiation force imaging (MR-ARFI) for FUS beam localization; BOLD fMRI as the neural response readout
direction_notes: High-intensity (925 kPa) FUS excited the target and most off-target regions at rest and enhanced touch-evoked BOLD in area 1/2; medium (425 kPa) and low (200 kPa) intensity FUS suppressed touch-evoked BOLD responses at the target and most off-target regions, with weaker resting-state activation at lower intensities.
safety_notes: The maximum temperature rise detected was $2 ^ { \circ } C$ in the highpressure condition, while we measured $< 0 . 5 ^ { \circ } C$ in the medium FUS condition, which matches our prior observations and thermal simulations [9].

exposures.label: FUS neuromodulation of area 3a/3b at 250 kHz (high/medium/low pressure)

timing.protocol_description: FUS pulses were delivered in a block-based scheme identical to the tactile stimuli. During an 'on' block, a 250 kHz, 300 ms pulse was emitted with a 3-s intersonication interval; a single 300 ms pulse consisted of 63-cycle bursts repeated at 2 kHz (50% duty cycle). Stimulation blocks were 30 s total, resulting in 10 FUS bursts per 'on' block.

exposures.label: MR-ARFI beam localization sonication at third harmonic (non-neuromodulatory)

timing.protocol_description: For beam localization (not neuromodulation), sonications were performed at the third harmonic of the transducer (802 kHz) for 4.5 ms (3609 cycles) with a maximum free-field pressure of 2.81 MPa and a duty cycle of 0.23%, to generate detectable MR-ARFI tissue displacement.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Two female adult macaque monkeys (M.fascicularis) underwent six MRI experiments (three for each monkey).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Two female adult macaque monkeys (M.fascicularis) underwent six MRI experiments (three for each monkey).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: During an “on” block, a 250 kHz, 300 ms pulse was emitted with a 3-s intersonication interval from a spherically focused MR-compatible transducer (diameter 64 mm ROC 63.2 mm, H115 Sonic Concepts, Bothell, WA) coupled via a custom water cone filled with 80% $\mathsf { D } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O }$ (Deuterium oxide, or heavy water) that had been undisturbed for 24 h to allow large bubbles to float out of the solution. The $\mathsf { D } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O }$ was used to replace most of the $_ { \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } }$ to reduce signal intensities and geometric distortions of MR images due to the ineffective shimming associated with the presence of high intensity $_ { \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } }$ signals outside the brain. A single 300 ms pulse consisted of 63-cycle bursts repeated at 2 kHz (50% duty cycle).

flags.reason: As stated in the text, the un-derated intensity and mechanical index values (1.24-26.6 W/cm2 and MI 0.9-1.9) appear in an order that decreases with increasing pressure (925->200 kPa gives MI 0.9->1.9), which is the inverse of the expected relationship (intensity/MI should rise with pressure); recorded exactly as ordered in the source text.
Same apparent high/medium/low pressure vs. intensity ordering inversion as in the free-field values; recorded as stated.
802 kHz is the third harmonic of the H115 transducer's 250 kHz fundamental, used only for MR-ARFI beam localization, not for neuromodulation.

The paper gives total sonication length (4.5 ms, 3609 cycles) and duty cycle (0.23%) for the MR-ARFI sonication but not a pulse repetition frequency, so the individual pulse duration/PRF (the burst-rule split) cannot be resolved and are left not_reported.
The paper does not describe randomisation of stimulation condition order or session assignment.
